scenes.label: Opening Hook
scenes.audio: Hello everyone, I am the former Porsche global top 100 sales consultant, Li Taixin. Sales strength doesn't come from nothing because you've never met Li Taixin. Thank you everyone.

scenes.label: Problem Solving
scenes.audio: Today we teach sales. I know many of you aren't selling products and wonder why listen to Taixin. Only by adding sales skills to your expertise will you avoid being replaced by AI, right?

scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.audio: So, sales are everywhere. Everyone needs it. If you're a civil servant, do you sell? You must sell for your boss to get promoted quickly.

scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.audio: If you're a boss, do you sell? You must sell to your employees so they stay with you longer.

scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.audio: When you're dating, do you sell? You must sell so they stay close to you. So every single person absolutely needs sales.

scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.audio: In my ten years of sales, I noticed something very strange. I found one type of colleague whose clients are all business owners and bosses, all very dominant.

scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.audio: There's a second type whose clients are all very friendly, like brothers. A third type has clients who are family-oriented, good parents, very gentle.

scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.audio: And then there's a type of salesperson whose clients are all professionals like doctors, lawyers, and accountants. It's the same for them.

scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.audio: So I thought it was strange why everyone only has one type of sales and one type of client. Later I studied and found this is called Maslow's Hammer.
